(Representative Image: Pexels) The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) will release Class 10 and 12 date sheet 2027 soon. Students who are appearing for the board exam will be able to download the subject-wise CBSE date sheet 2027 and timings on the official website, cbse.gov.in. 
 CBSE 2026 Class 10 Second Board Exam QP's:  Math |  Math Std. |  English |  Science 
 Chapter-wise Ques:  Science |  Maths |  PYQ's | Formula & Notes:  Science |  Maths 
 Mid Term Question Paper:  English |  Maths |  Social Science |  Science 
 The board has completed the regular submission window for the CBSE 2027 candidate list submission for the 2026-27 academic session. The  LOC submission window with late fees has also closed on October 30. Students can expect the CBSE board exam date 2027 any day now.
 Based on previous years’ trends, the CBSE Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations are expected to be held in February and March 2027. Meanwhile, CBSE has also released sample question papers for Classes 10 and 12 for 2026 to 27 on its website, cbseacademic.nic.in.

 CBSE Board Exam Dates 2027: Download steps
 When CBSE releases the Class 10 and Class 12 timetable, students can follow these steps to download the CBSE exam timetable PDF. 
 Visit the official CBSE website, cbse.gov.in
 On the homepage, find the latest announcements section
 Find and click on the link for ‘CBSE Class 10 or Class 12 date sheet 2027’
 The examination timetable PDF will pop up on the screen
 Download the date sheet and save it for future use
 Students should start preparing while waiting for the CBSE board exam schedule 2027.
 CBSE Board Exams 2027: Passing marks
 CBSE Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations will require students to secure at least 33 percent marks in each subject to pass. Students who do not meet the minimum passing criteria can be eligible for improvement or supplementary examinations, depending on the CBSE rules.
 Class 10 students can appear in session 2 to improve their scores in up to 3 subjects. Class 12 students will have the option of giving supplementary exams in case they fail to secure passing marks in the main board exams.
